author: Target builder workflow (corrected target contract; handoff items 1-9 supersede the master's all-20-mm prompt)
glutealConsequence: The exploratory 3-actuator gluteal compartment split would replace one target group with three, changing the campaign from 27 groups to 29. It is NOT approved by this contract (handoff item 6); the aggregate nine-compartment glut_max3 target (4867 N stock group MIF) remains the baseline. Adopting the split later would require a new, explicit approval and a re-derivation of the layer schedule and group count downstream.

layerOrder.basis: Starts from MASTER_DIRECTIVE_20261103.md item 5 provisional order. One documented adjustment, grounded in handoff item 7 (not a layering-table result): psoas (27) and iliacus (26) are solved as ONE coupled junction pair at the head of the trunk/deep-hip region because they share an attachment/load-transfer junction. The geometry extraction's layering table was NOT available on easteregg2 on 2026-11-03 (searched Functional_Routing_20261027/, tmp/functional_routing_20261103/, and Neuromechanical_Models/AH001_Simscape_Repair/packaging/), so NO bone-distance adjustments from that table could be applied; see unresolved[0].
layerOrder.rule: The deepest layer optimizes against bone; every later group treats ALL earlier layers' occupied envelopes as hard obstacles. After the first full pass, run coordinated refinement so an early poor choice cannot permanently block later muscles (master item 5).

trunk/deep hip.notes: psoas(27)+iliacus(26) coupled junction pair first; then erector spinae (1); internal oblique (2) BEFORE external oblique (3) per the provisional order.

thigh.notes: vas_int/combined vasti (11) and biceps femoris short head (10) first (deep, before superficial crossing groups); then adductor group (25), semimem (5), biceps femoris long head (4), rectus femoris (8), gracilis (9), sartorius (6), TFL (7); gluteal replacement group (24) last, as its local corridors permit.

lower leg.notes: Posterior deep corridor first: tib_post (15), flex_dig (20), flex_hal (21). Lateral corridor: per_brev (17) BEFORE per_long (18). Superficial posterior: soleus (12) before med_gas (13)/lat_gas (14). Anterior corridor: tib_ant (16), ext_dig (22), ext_hal (23), per_tert (19) placed in their appropriate anterior/lateral corridors; corridor separation makes some cross-corridor pairs order-independent - resolve with the (missing) layering table.

centerlineConstraint: No attachment point may cross the pelvis-frame centerline z=0 (HARDWARE_AND_ZCODE_HANDOFF.md item 8, verbatim requirement). Side ownership is assigned from the seed/model (right side, per actuator_map_27 'one_side': the right side is optimized and the left is its mirror). Every candidate attachment point AND mechanical mount anchor is transformed into the pelvis frame at every evaluated pose, and sideSign*z_pelvis >= 0 is enforced as a hard constraint. Sign flips and absolute coordinates are forbidden after optimization. Any seed lying on the centerline is resolved explicitly before search; it may never switch sides during optimization.
xiSource: Xi0-Xi3 only; Xi4 is WAIVED (handoff item 9). Sources read 2026-11-03: (a) Code/Matlab/Mesh_Optimization/buildKneeFlexorContext20mm.m lines 178-202: pick=77 from minimizeFlxPin10_results_20260908_2brkt_2trans_noT3.mat filtered_results with xCols=[4 5 6] -> Xi0=3.94 mm, Xi1=3.998e4 N/m, Xi2=1.473e4 N/m; Xi3 taken from the extensor flxr77 front row 32 (lines 188-190). (b) Code/Matlab/Mesh_Optimization/buildKneeExtContext20mm.m lines 162-183: pick=32 from minimizeExt10mmX3_results_20260920_flxr77.mat with xCols=[5 6 7 8], Xi1/Xi2 LOCKED to the flexor row-77 pair. (c) Verified this ask in MATLAB against the mats of record: minimizeFlxPin10_results.mat row 77 (xCols 4/5/6) = Xi0=0.00393737 m, Xi1=39978.7 N/m, Xi2=14733.8 N/m; minimizeExt10mmX3_results.mat row 32 (xCols 5/6/7/8) = Xi0=-0.00637802 m, Xi1=39978.7 N/m, Xi2=14733.8 N/m, Xi3=0.158289; lock-check flexor Xi1/Xi2 == extensor Xi1/Xi2 = TRUE (one shared pair across flexor and extensor, advisor requirement). These encode the dissertation Appendix C conventions: Xi0 = bracket offset/compliance length scale; Xi1/Xi2 = effective system-stiffness parameters (NOT literal bracket beam stiffness - AGENTS.md 2026-09-07 semantics), with the evaluator's mixed two-bracket convention (insertion/tibia bracket one-rotation pitch-only K=[X1,X2,X1], origin/hip bracket two-rotation K2=[X1,X1,X2], since 2026-09-13); Xi3 = wrapping-loss factor (dimensionless, flexor carry 0.158289). Xi1 direction assignment per bracket follows the configuration-dependent anisotropic table in Chapter 30/Appendix C; no fifth factor is invented or renamed.

contraction.note: Handoff item 2. No universal 25% contraction limit; flag extrapolation outside the experimental force-contraction domain.

diameter_endpoints.10mm: Resting diameter 10 mm; inflated/fully-contracted diameter must come from the 10 mm sleeve's OWN calibration. NEVER apply the 20 mm diameter law to a 10 mm sleeve (handoff item 2). The 10 mm calibration was not located in this ask - unresolved[3].
diameter_endpoints.note: Fully inflated 20 mm Festo BPA diameter used for clearance geometry in the context builders is 38.5 mm (buildKneeExtContext20mm.m 'geo.bpaRadius = 0.0385/2'); the 38 mm endpoint above is the handoff's calibrated endpoint.

limits.restingLength: Resting length excludes end fittings; packaging includes both fittings (master item 2).
limits.offAxisTorquePenalty: NONE (handoff item 9 / master item 8). Secondary crossed-DOF torques are recorded for inspection only and are never penalized, including inherited terms disguised as another regularizer. Structural mount reactions still matter for sizing and compliance; they are not off-axis torque penalties.
limits.bpaBpaOverlap: SOFT penalty (handoff item 9): BPA-BPA interference is a penalty, not a universal hard clearance constraint. Compute overlap from pose-dependent inflated envelopes, evaluate only physically simultaneous configurations, and report overlap depth and extent.
limits.footOccupancy: No BPA body, end fitting, or tackle block may occupy the foot (handoff item 9 / master item 6). Tendons may route through and terminate on the foot.

tendonSpanPlaceholders.minFootTendonSpan_note: PLACEHOLDER - implementer computes from geometry: minimum tendon/Bowden length for every foot-actuating route, from the required ankle-to-insertion routing and hardware clearance over the full ankle/subtalar/MTP motion range (master item 6). No arbitrary token tendon length that lets a sleeve extend onto the foot.
tendonSpanPlaceholders.minKneeTendonSpan_note: PLACEHOLDER - implementer computes from geometry: minimum artificial-tendon/Bowden span needed across the knee over the robot knee range 0 to -120 deg (no hyperextension), packaging brackets, housing stops, ferrules, cable exits, articulation, and minimum bend radius through the sweep (master items 2 and 6). For long knee-crossing actuators consider pinned proximal and distal BPA sections with the central crossing carried by tendon/Bowden; initialize equal halves and parameterize any optimized split.

limits.rom: Robot knee range 0 to -120 deg, no hyperextension; other coordinates per actuator_map_27 rom_table_deg.
